### alt
Usage: alt [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  portable     Transfer signed repository snapshots with explicit cutover and durable request recovery
  auth         Sign in to a server through explicit browser device consent
  runner       Inspect tools or execute one immutable validation snapshot
  task         Record an authorized task in an isolated workspace
  candidate    Capture and inspect immutable candidates and complete input identities
  evidence     Preserve validation reports and inspect their current validity
  request      Inspect durable whole-command receipts without executing the command
  cat-file     Provide contents or details of repository objects
  rev-parse    Pick out and massage parameters
  log          Show commit logs
  reflog       Show the log of a ref: the commits it was at, the latest first
  intake       Verify and independently import a supported Git source for tasks
  import       Import this git repository into a .alt store
  export       Export this .alt store back to a git repository
  init         Create an empty native .alt repository
  add          Stage file contents into the index
  commit       Record staged changes as a new commit
  status       Show the working tree status
  branch       List, create, or delete branches
  switch       Switch branches, materializing the target tree into the work tree
  restore      Restore files of the working tree, entries of the index, or both
  checkout     Switch branches, or restore files of the working tree
  reset        Move the current branch to a commit, or reset index entries
  rm           Remove files from the index and the working tree
  mv           Move or rename a file or a directory
  stash        Put away what is not committed, and bring it back
  show         Show a commit: header + per-file unified diff against its first parent
  blame        Line-by-line origin attribution for one file (`git blame`-style)
  meta         Show or change the metadata recorded with a commit (kept in git notes under refs/notes/alt/meta; the commit itself never changes)
  lfs          Git LFS: the large contents behind the pointer files LFS paths commit
  bisect       Find the commit that introduced a change by binary search
  rebase       Replay the current branch's own commits onto another base
  revert       Record new commits that undo earlier ones
  cherry-pick  Apply the changes from a commit on top of the current branch
  config       Read or update git-style config keys (`user.name`, …)
  tag          List, create (lightweight or annotated), or delete tags
  diff         Show changes between the index, the working tree and commits
  merge        Join another branch into the current one
  flow         git-flow workflow operations (atomic, undoable)
  undo         Undo the last branch/HEAD operation (inverts one op log entry)
  operation    Inspect and finish interrupted local operations
  workspace    Manage parallel workspaces (isolated HEAD/index/working tree)
  remote       Manage git remotes (persisted as `<alt-dir>/remotes/<name>`)
  clone        Clone a remote repository: init + remote add origin + fetch + checkout
  fetch        Fetch refs + objects from a configured remote (git smart-http v2)
  push         Push refs + objects to a configured remote (git smart-http v1)
  identity     Manage local identities + trusted public keys
  op-log       Audit-view the op log: who did what, in order, with the parsed principal and any ref changes carried in each op's payload
  ci           alt-CI workflow inspection. Subcommand surface; `alt ci validate` runs the schema-tier lint
  fsck         Read and verify every record the repository stores: each chunk, blob and object against its hash, each index against the file it indexes, the whole operation log, and the refs against a replay of that log. Exits non-zero at the first record that fails
  verify       Verify the `alt-sig` header on one or more commit objects. With no args, walks the current branch's commit chain back to root (newest first). Each row is one of: `signed-ok:<principal>` / `unsigned` / `bad-sig:<principal>` / `untrusted:<principal>`
  prompt       Print the state of the repository for a shell prompt
  shell        Print the plugin that completes alt commands and shows the repository's state in a shell

Options:
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
  -V, --version                Print version
### alt portable
Transfer signed repository snapshots with explicit cutover and durable request recovery

Usage: alt portable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  export           Download a complete signed snapshot without stopping source writes
  export-status    Inspect the same immutable source export
  freeze-source    Stop source writes only at the original export watermark
  reopen-source    Explicitly remove the original source write barrier
  retire-export    Release retention for the original export; a frozen source must be reopened first
  import           Verify a local archive and stage it privately in a new empty target repository
  import-status    Query the original target intent, including a lost activation response
  activate-import  Atomically activate the original staged import under current target authority
  abandon-import   Abandon a receiving import without deleting the source or accepted history

Options:
      --json                   
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt portable export
Download a complete signed snapshot without stopping source writes

Usage: alt portable export [OPTIONS] --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE> --journal <JOURNAL> --repository <REPOSITORY> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE>
          Private credential created by alt auth login
      --journal <JOURNAL>
          Private durable journal; reuse this directory after an interrupted attempt
      --max-metadata-bytes <MAX_METADATA_BYTES>
          [default: 16777216]
      --max-entries <MAX_ENTRIES>
          [default: 1000000]
      --max-publications <MAX_PUBLICATIONS>
          [default: 100000]
      --max-blob-bytes <MAX_BLOB_BYTES>
          [default: 8589934592]
      --max-total-bytes <MAX_TOTAL_BYTES>
          [default: 68719476736]
      --timeout-seconds <TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          [default: 120]
      --repository <REPOSITORY>
          
      --json
          
      --output <OUTPUT>
          
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>
          Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>
          Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help
          Print help

### alt portable import
Verify a local archive and stage it privately in a new empty target repository

Usage: alt portable import [OPTIONS] --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE> --journal <JOURNAL> --repository <REPOSITORY> --archive <ARCHIVE> --mappings <MAPPINGS> --source-installation <SOURCE_INSTALLATION> --source-repository <SOURCE_REPOSITORY> --source-epoch <SOURCE_EPOCH> --source-key <SOURCE_KEY>

Options:
      --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE>
          Private credential created by alt auth login
      --journal <JOURNAL>
          Private durable journal; reuse this directory after an interrupted attempt
      --max-metadata-bytes <MAX_METADATA_BYTES>
          [default: 16777216]
      --max-entries <MAX_ENTRIES>
          [default: 1000000]
      --max-publications <MAX_PUBLICATIONS>
          [default: 100000]
      --max-blob-bytes <MAX_BLOB_BYTES>
          [default: 8589934592]
      --max-total-bytes <MAX_TOTAL_BYTES>
          [default: 68719476736]
      --timeout-seconds <TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          [default: 120]
      --repository <REPOSITORY>
          
      --archive <ARCHIVE>
          
      --json
          
      --mappings <MAPPINGS>
          JSON list of explicit source identity dispositions; null links preserve history only
      --source-installation <SOURCE_INSTALLATION>
          
      --source-repository <SOURCE_REPOSITORY>
          
      --source-epoch <SOURCE_EPOCH>
          
      --source-key <SOURCE_KEY>
          Source receipt public key obtained independently of the archive
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>
          Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>
          Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help
          Print help

### alt auth
Sign in to a server through explicit browser device consent

Usage: alt auth [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  delegate      Give an agent a short credential with explicit repository and write bounds
  delegations   List agent credentials belonging to the current human account
  revoke-agent  Revoke one agent credential owned by the current human account
  login         Save a private, origin-bound credential after explicit browser consent
  status        Check the current principal and installation without printing secrets
  logout        Revoke the saved credential before removing its private file

Options:
      --json                   
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt auth delegate
Give an agent a short credential with explicit repository and write bounds

Usage: alt auth delegate [OPTIONS] --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE> --agent-file <AGENT_FILE>

Options:
      --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE>
          
      --agent-file <AGENT_FILE>
          
      --plan <PLAN>
          JSON purpose, agent_session, lifetime_seconds and scope
      --resume
          Retry the same privately saved delegation after interruption
      --json
          
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>
          Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>
          Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help
          Print help

      --server <SERVER>
          
      --credential-file <CREDENTIAL_FILE>
          
      --resume
          Continue the same saved request after interruption
      --no-wait
          Save the request and print its public confirmation URL without polling
      --allow-loopback-http
          
      --json
          
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>
          Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>
          Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository

### alt task
Record an authorized task in an isolated workspace

Usage: alt task [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  remote               Publish selected task history or receive and continue published work
  changes              Show the complete candidate diff against the task baseline
  review               Record explicit review of a current candidate and its observed evidence
  review-show          
  integrate            Atomically integrate a reviewed candidate into its unoccupied target
  integration-show     
  integration-collect  Collect an already recorded ref transaction without applying it again
  export               Export a completed integration to a verified independent Git directory
  delivery-show        
  delivery-collect     Verify an existing delivery after a lost publication response
  create               Record a task definition and current isolated-workspace baseline
  list                 
  show                 
  abandon              Append an abandonment record; keep candidates, logs and workspace files

Options:
      --json                   
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt task remote
Publish selected task history or receive and continue published work

Usage: alt task remote [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  changes  Inspect and publish exact associations with Sentori
  connect  Bind an HTTPS origin, repository and operator-provided receipt key
  preview  Freeze the exact records, attachments and optional ref updates to publish
  publish  Send or resume an already previewed publication using its original ID
  attest   Sign the original completed evidence statement with a collector key
  review   Download the complete ready selection for an independent current review
  approve  Approve the exact previously inspected request as the current reviewer
  status   Query the authoritative outcome without sending a new publication
  list     List published roots, or the signed publications containing a root
  receive  Receive an explicitly selected signed publication; never execute it
  adopt    Accept a received task in this isolated workspace with its original ID

Options:
      --json                   
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt task remote changes
Inspect and publish exact associations with Sentori

Usage: alt task remote changes [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  channels       List the explicitly configured Sentori channels
  list           List historical facts and their current delivery state
  show           Read an original signed fact under current repository permission
  repair         Inspect a repair request and any actually published native Task
  repair-create  Create a local Task from a currently authorized repair request
  preview        Save an exact Delivery mapping or withdrawal before sending it
  send           Send or resume a saved association using its original request
  status         Query a saved association without creating a new request
  reauthorize    Explicitly resume a pending statement with this actor's current credential

Options:
      --json                   
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

  <DIGEST>  

Options:
      --definition <DEFINITION>
          Normal TaskSpec JSON; source is supplied by the verified request
      --target <TARGET>

      --json

### alt task remote changes reauthorize
Explicitly resume a pending statement with this actor's current credential

Usage: alt task remote changes reauthorize [OPTIONS] <REMOTE> <CHANNEL> <DIGEST>

Arguments:
  <REMOTE>   
  <CHANNEL>  
  <DIGEST>

### alt rev-parse
Pick out and massage parameters

Usage: alt rev-parse [OPTIONS] [REV]...

Arguments:
  [REV]...  Revisions to resolve: an id, a ref, `HEAD~2`, `HEAD^2`, `v1^{commit}`, `@{u}`, `<rev>:<path>`, or `:<path>` and `:<n>:<path>` for what the index has, at stage n

Options:
      --show-toplevel          Print the root of the working tree
      --git-dir                Print the directory the repository is kept in: `.alt` from the root of its tree, else in full
      --absolute-git-dir       Print the directory the repository is kept in, in full
      --show-prefix            Print where the command runs, from the root of the tree
      --is-inside-work-tree    Print `true`: the command runs in a working tree
      --abbrev-ref             Print the short name of the branch or ref a revision is, where it is one: `main` for `HEAD`, `origin/main` for `@{u}`
      --symbolic-full-name     Print the full name of the ref a revision is, where it is one
      --short[=<LENGTH>]       Print ids shortened to as many digits as tell them apart, at least LENGTH of them
      --verify                 Take one revision and fail where it names no object
  -q, --quiet                  With --verify, say nothing where the revision names no object
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt log
Show commit logs

Usage: alt log [OPTIONS] [REV]... [-- <PATHS>...]

Arguments:
  [REV]...         start revision, or a range: `A..B` for what leads to B and not to A, `A...B` for what leads to one of them and not to both; then paths, to show only the commits that change them [default: HEAD]
  [-- <PATHS>...]  paths, where a word before them could be taken for a revision

Options:
      --pretty <PRETTY>        pretty-print commits: raw | oneline (ignored with --json) [default: oneline]
  -n <MAX_COUNT>               limit the number of commits
      --json                   emit the commit list as a stable JSON object
  -p, --patch                  show a per-commit patch (unified diff for text, compact chunk + perceptual summary for binary so large-file history doesn't blow up the terminal). Ignored with --json
      --cc                     with -p, show for a merge commit the combined diff of what the merge itself changed (hunks that differ from every parent)
      --oneline                each commit as its abbreviated id and its subject
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

### alt add
Stage file contents into the index

Usage: alt add [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Paths to stage; `.` stages the directory the command runs in

Options:
      --renormalize            Store every tracked file among the paths again, as the attributes and line-ending settings now in force clean it
  -f, --force                  Stage files that an ignore rule hides as well
  -u, --update                 Stage what changed in the files the index has, and no new file: in the whole tree when no path is given
  -A, --all                    Stage every change, new files as well: in the whole tree when no path is given
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human line
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt commit
Record staged changes as a new commit

Usage: alt commit [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -m <MESSAGE>                 Commit message (with --amend, defaults to the amended commit's)
      --amend                  Replace the current branch tip with a new commit made from the index, keeping its parents and author
      --no-edit                Keep the amended commit's message (alt never opens an editor, so this is already the default without -m; accepted as in git)
      --allow-empty            Record the commit even when it changes nothing
  -n, --no-verify              Skip the pre-commit checks (secret scan, large-file warning)
      --validate               Only run the pre-commit checks on what is staged; commit nothing
      --decision <TEXT>        Record a one-line decision in the commit's metadata (up to 3)
      --meta <KEY=VALUE>       Record an extra metadata field (`key=value`, e.g. `model=…`)
      --json                   Emit the new commit/tree oids (or, with --validate, the findings) as a JSON object
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

      --json                      Emit a stable JSON object instead of the human-readable view

### alt restore
Restore files of the working tree, entries of the index, or both

Usage: alt restore [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Paths to restore; `.` is the directory the command runs in

Options:
  -S, --staged                 Restore the index, from HEAD unless a source is given
  -W, --worktree               Restore the files; what is restored where --staged is not given
  -s, --source <REV>           The commit to restore from: the index for the files alone, else HEAD, where none is given
      --ours                   For a path in conflict, restore the file of the current branch
      --theirs                 For a path in conflict, restore the file of the branch merged in
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of printing nothing
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt checkout
Switch branches, or restore files of the working tree

Usage: alt checkout [OPTIONS] [NAMES]... [-- <PATHS>...]

Arguments:
  [NAMES]...       A branch to switch to, or paths to restore from the index; a revision before the paths restores them from it, index and files
  [-- <PATHS>...]  Paths to restore, where a name before them could be taken for a branch or a revision

Options:
  -b                           Create the branch named before switching to it
      --ours                   For a path in conflict, check out the file of the current branch
      --theirs                 For a path in conflict, check out the file of the branch merged in
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human line
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt reset
Move the current branch to a commit, or reset index entries

Usage: alt reset [OPTIONS] [NAMES]... [-- <PATHS>...]

Arguments:
  [NAMES]...       The commit to reset to, HEAD where none is given, and paths: with paths, their index entries are reset and nothing else
  [-- <PATHS>...]  Paths, where a name before them could be taken for a revision

Options:
      --soft                   Move the branch and leave the index and the files as they are
      --mixed                  Move the branch and reset the index; the files stay (the default)
      --hard                   Move the branch and reset the index and the files
  -q, --quiet                  Say nothing of what is left unstaged or where HEAD is
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt rm
Remove files from the index and the working tree

Usage: alt rm [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Files to remove; a directory only with -r

Options:
      --cached                 Remove the index entries and leave the files
  -r                           Remove what lies beneath a directory given
  -f, --force                  Remove a file whose changes are nowhere else as well
      --ignore-unmatch         Pass over a path that names no file of the index
  -n, --dry-run                Say what would be removed and remove nothing
  -q, --quiet                  Do not say what is removed
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt mv
Move or rename a file or a directory

Usage: alt mv [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  The file or directory to rename and its new name, or what to move and the directory to move it into

Options:
  -f, --force                  Write over a file at the new name
  -k                           Pass over a source that cannot be moved
  -n, --dry-run                Say what would be renamed and rename nothing
  -v, --verbose                Say each rename
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt stash
Put away what is not committed, and bring it back

Usage: alt stash [OPTIONS] [WORDS]... [-- <PATHS>...]

Arguments:
  [WORDS]...       What to do: push (the default), list, show, apply, pop, drop or clear; then the entry it is done to, as `stash@{1}` or `1`, the latest where none is named, or after push the paths to put away
  [-- <PATHS>...]  With push: the paths to put away and no other

Options:
  -m, --message <MESSAGE>      With push: the message of the entry
  -u, --include-untracked      With push: put the untracked files away as well
      --index                  With apply and pop: bring back as staged what was staged
  -p, --patch                  With show: the patch of the entry instead of the summary
  -q, --quiet                  Do not say what was saved, applied or dropped
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt show
Show a commit: header + per-file unified diff against its first parent

Usage: alt show [OPTIONS] [REV]

Arguments:
  [REV]  Revision to show (default `HEAD`). Accepts any spec `rev-parse` resolves

Options:
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON diff instead of unified text
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt blame
Line-by-line origin attribution for one file (`git blame`-style)

Usage: alt blame [OPTIONS] <PATH> [REV]

Arguments:
  <PATH>  Path to the file to blame (relative to the current directory)
  [REV]   Revision to start the walk from (default `HEAD`)

Options:
  -M                           Trace lines moved within the file. A number against the letter is how many letters and digits they must carry (20 if absent)
      --follow                 Accepted for command lines written before renames were always followed; it changes nothing
  -C                           Trace lines copied from files changed in the same commit; twice, from any file when the blamed file is created; three times, from any file in every commit. Implies -M. A number against the letter works as for -M (40 if absent)
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

### alt bisect
Find the commit that introduced a change by binary search

Usage: alt bisect [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start  Start a session, optionally naming the bad commit and good ones
  bad    Mark commits (default: the one being tested) as bad
  good   Mark commits (default: the one being tested) as good
  skip   Mark commits (default: the one being tested) as untestable
  reset  End the session and go back to the branch
  run    Let a command judge each commit: exit 0 good, 125 skip, 1-127 bad, anything else stops

Options:
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

      --continue               Commit the resolved step and go on
      --skip                   Drop the stopped step and go on
      --abort                  Put the branch back as it was before the rebase

      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository

      --continue               Commit the resolved revert and go on with the rest
      --abort                  Put the branch back where it was before the reverts
      --no-edit                Use the generated message (alt never opens an editor; accepted as in git)
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one

### alt config
Read or update git-style config keys (`user.name`, …)

Usage: alt config [OPTIONS] [KEY] [VALUE]

Arguments:
  [KEY]    Dotted key (e.g. `user.name`). Omit when `--list` or `--unset` is set
  [VALUE]  New value. When supplied, the key is set (overwriting any existing value); when omitted, the key is read

Options:
      --list                   List every entry as `section.key=value` (git's default `--list` shape)
      --unset <UNSET>          Remove a key from the config file
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt tag
List, create (lightweight or annotated), or delete tags

Usage: alt tag [OPTIONS] [NAME] [REV]

Arguments:
  [NAME]  Tag name to create. Omit (and omit `-d`) to list all tags
  [REV]   Revision the new tag should point to (default HEAD). Only honoured when creating a tag

Options:
  -d, --delete <DELETE>        Delete a tag by name. Mutually exclusive with `name`
  -a, --annotate               Create an *annotated* tag (writes a tag object carrying the message + tagger ident, instead of a bare ref)
  -m, --message <MESSAGE>      Annotated-tag message. Required when `-a` is set
      --json                   JSON output for list mode (ignored otherwise)
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt diff
Show changes between the index, the working tree and commits

Usage: alt diff [OPTIONS] [REVS]... [-- <PATHS>...]

Arguments:
  [REVS]...        What to compare: nothing for the index and the files; one commit for that commit and the files; two commits, or `A..B`, for one and the other; `A...B` for what B changed since the two parted
  [-- <PATHS>...]  Only what changed at these paths

Options:
      --cached                 Compare with the index in place of the files: HEAD, or the commit given, against what is staged [aliases: --staged]
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON diff instead of unified text
      --semantic               Show an AST-level diff per supported language: item-level logical vs format-only changes for `.rs` files; line/binary diff for files without a parser
      --name-only              Print the path of each file that changed and nothing else
      --name-status            Print a letter for how each file changed, and its path
      --stat                   Print how many lines changed in each file, and in all
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt merge
Join another branch into the current one

Usage: alt merge [OPTIONS] [BRANCH]

Arguments:
  [BRANCH]  Branch, or any other commit, to merge into the current branch

Options:
      --abort                  Put the index and the files back as they were before the merge
      --no-ff                  Record a merge commit even where the branch could be fast-forwarded
      --ff-only                Fast-forward or change nothing: refuse a merge that needs a commit
      --no-edit                Take the message of the merge commit as it is (alt never opens an editor, so this is already the default; accepted as in git)
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human lines
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

### alt clone

Arguments:

  [DIR]  Destination directory (defaults to the URL's last path segment with any `.git` suffix stripped)

      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository

### alt fetch
Fetch refs + objects from a configured remote (git smart-http v2)

Usage: alt fetch [OPTIONS] [REMOTE] [REFSPECS]...

Arguments:
  [REMOTE]       Remote name (defaults to `origin`) [default: origin]
  [REFSPECS]...  Refspecs to fetch (defaults to the remote's configured refspec)

Options:
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human view
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt push
Push refs + objects to a configured remote (git smart-http v1)

Usage: alt push [OPTIONS] [REMOTE] [REFSPECS]...

Arguments:
  [REMOTE]       Remote name (defaults to `origin`) [default: origin]
  [REFSPECS]...  Refspecs to push (`<src>:<dst>` or just `<src>` — defaults to the current branch onto its same-named remote branch)

Options:
  -f, --force                  Force the update (allow non-fast-forward); the server still enforces its own policy
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human view
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt identity
Manage local identities + trusted public keys

Usage: alt identity [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init   Generate a new Ed25519 keypair under `<alt-dir>/identity/<principal>.{pub,sec}`
  list   List installed identities (no secret material; only `.pub` rows)
  trust  Add a public key to the trust store (`<alt-dir>/trust/<principal>.pub`)

Options:
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human view
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

Generate a new Ed25519 keypair under `<alt-dir>/identity/<principal>.{pub,sec}`

Usage: alt identity init [OPTIONS] [PRINCIPAL]

Arguments:
  [PRINCIPAL]  Principal id (defaults to `$ALT_PRINCIPAL_ID` or `$USER`)

Options:
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON result instead of the human view
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help

Usage: alt identity trust [OPTIONS] <PRINCIPAL> <PUB_FILE>

  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt op-log
Audit-view the op log: who did what, in order, with the parsed principal and any ref changes carried in each op's payload

Usage: alt op-log [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n <MAX_COUNT>               Limit the number of entries shown (newest first; default = all)
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON list instead of the human view
      --verify                 Check each op against the signature sidecar + trust store; rows tagged `signed-ok` / `unsigned` / `bad-sig` / `untrusted`
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt ci

Commands:

Options:
      --json                   Emit line-delimited JSON diagnostics instead of the human `<path>:<line>:<col>: <severity>: <message>` form
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt ci validate
Validate one or more `workflow.toml` files against the alt-CI schema. With no arguments, scans `.alt/ci/*/workflow.toml`

Usage: alt ci validate [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Specific `workflow.toml` files to check (default: scan `.alt/ci/<name>/workflow.toml`)

Options:
      --json                   Emit line-delimited JSON diagnostics instead of the human `<path>:<line>:<col>: <severity>: <message>` form
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt fsck
Read and verify every record the repository stores: each chunk, blob and object against its hash, each index against the file it indexes, the whole operation log, and the refs against a replay of that log. Exits non-zero at the first record that fails

Usage: alt fsck [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json                   Emit the record counts as a JSON object
      --drop-lost              List the records of the object store that name content which is not stored, wherever they lie, and what names the objects that go with them; with --yes, take those records out
      --yes                    With --drop-lost: take the records out
      --committed              With --drop-lost --yes: take the records out also where a commit that a ref reaches names an object that goes with them
      --no-connectivity        Leave out the walk from every ref through commits and trees, which finds the objects they name that are not stored
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt verify
Verify the `alt-sig` header on one or more commit objects. With no args, walks the current branch's commit chain back to root (newest first). Each row is one of: `signed-ok:<principal>` / `unsigned` / `bad-sig:<principal>` / `untrusted:<principal>`

Usage: alt verify [OPTIONS] [COMMITS]...

Arguments:
  [COMMITS]...  Commit oids to check (hex). Empty = walk HEAD

Options:
  -n, --max-count <MAX_COUNT>  Limit when walking HEAD (default 50; ignored when oids given)
      --json                   Emit a structured JSON list instead of the human view
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt prompt
Print the state of the repository for a shell prompt

Usage: alt prompt [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>        `lines` for a key and its value on each line, `zsh` for one line a zsh evaluates into the associative array `alt_prompt` [default: lines] [possible values: lines, zsh]
      --no-untracked           Do not look for untracked files
      --no-ahead-behind        Do not count commits against the remotes
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt shell
Print the plugin that completes alt commands and shows the repository's state in a shell

Usage: alt shell [OPTIONS] <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  The shell to print the plugin for [possible values: zsh]

Options:
      --completion             Print only the completion function, as the file `_alt` to put on `fpath`
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
### alt complete
Say what may stand at the cursor of a command line, for a shell

Usage: alt complete [OPTIONS] --shell <SHELL> --current <CURRENT> [WORDS]...

Arguments:
  [WORDS]...  The words of the command line, the program first

Options:
      --shell <SHELL>          The shell that asks [possible values: zsh]
      --current <CURRENT>      Which of the words the cursor is in, the program being word 0
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>  Operate in the named parallel workspace instead of the default one
      --request-id <HEX>       Stable request identity for a write in an existing native repository
  -h, --help                   Print help
